frameworks.name: Future‑Emotion Priming Framework
frameworks.summary: Pre‑experience desired future emotions through vivid mental rehearsal, signaling the body’s chemistry and genetics to align with the envisioned outcome.

Replace past‑driven emotional scripts with future‑oriented feelings (e.g., abundance, love) and rehearse them daily to fire‑wire new neural pathways.
Use short, focused meditation sessions to observe thoughts without judgment, turning the mind into a conscious observer rather than an automatic program.
Align your language and behavior with the person you want to become; consistently speak, act, and feel as if that future self already exists.
Commit to a daily micro‑practice—visualization, affirmation, or physical embodiment of the desired state—for at least 30 days to solidify the new circuitry.

frameworks.name: Open to Goal
frameworks.summary: Team members work until they hit a predefined target, regardless of time, encouraging relentless effort until the goal is achieved.

frameworks.name: Volume × Leverage Output Model
frameworks.summary: Output is calculated as the number of repetitions (volume) multiplied by the skill or effectiveness of each action (leverage), emphasizing both quantity and quality.

takeaways: Measure your work by the effort you put in, not by external applause; keep a personal scorecard that pushes you when no one is watching.
View pain as a natural indicator of activity, not a problem to avoid, and let it fuel continued action.
Focus on high‑volume, high‑skill repetitions (e.g., the Rule of 100) to build leverage and accelerate mastery.
Accept the lonely, uncomfortable chapter as a necessary part of growth and use criticism as proof you are moving beyond others' expectations.
Shift your goal from a specific outcome to the continuous process of emptying the tank—becoming the hardest‑working version of yourself.

frameworks.name: Stoic Tripartite System
frameworks.summary: Divides philosophy into physics (nature of the universe), logic (methods of truth), and ethics (application of knowledge to virtuous living).

frameworks.name: Dichotomy of Control
frameworks.summary: Distinguishes between things within our power (desires, judgments) and those outside it (health, wealth), directing effort toward internal mastery.

takeaways: Conduct a daily self‑examination of thoughts and actions to align with your inner virtues.
Focus your will on what you can control—desires, opinions, and actions—and accept external events with equanimity.
Treat external circumstances (wealth, health, reputation) as indifferent, using them as opportunities to practice virtue.
Lead by duty and humility, prioritizing the common good over personal glory or ambition.
When faced with injustice or suffering, respond with constructive goodness rather than retaliation, echoing both stoic and Christian ideals.
